feed.title: What does "post-quantum" actually mean for a Bitcoin L2 when settlement still happens on a non-PQ L1?

entry.title: What does "post-quantum" actually mean for a Bitcoin L2 when settlement still happens on a non-PQ L1?
entry.summary:
The discussion emphasizes the importance of focusing on security aspects when developing a post-quantum (PQ) resistant layer 2 (L2) solution atop a blockchain layer 1 (L1) that itself lacks PQ resistance. A key point raised is the vulnerability of bridge components in such architectures, which are often the most susceptible to attacks. This vulnerability necessitates heightened attention during development to ensure robustness against potential security breaches.
Another significant aspect covered is the challenges associated with peg-in mechanisms in the context of PQ resistance. It is argued that ensuring the PQ resistance of the peg-in process is crucial before advancing further considerations about the subsequent stages of blockchain interactions. This necessity serves as a driver for innovation, urging developers to explore and implement PQ-resistant solutions at the initial stages of transaction handling.
The conversation also touches upon the use of one-time signatures (OTS) and their implications in transaction verification within hash-based schemes. Concerns are highlighted regarding the verification logic and potential issues such as front-running, where the visibility of transaction details before processing could be exploited maliciously. These points underline the need for careful design and consideration of unintended consequences in cryptographic implementations.
Finally, the narrative advocates for leveraging existing protocols to maximize their potential before considering more drastic measures like forking. The speaker acknowledges personal limitations in fully addressing all technical questions, pointing to a broader need for ongoing education and research. There is a strong call to action for building upon the current infrastructure, specifically Bitcoin, to foster development and application of new technologies in the blockchain space. This approach not only addresses immediate concerns but also paves the way for future advancements.
